newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end higher, led by small-cap shares.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end higher, led by small-cap shares.

text.p: Shares ended Friday's trading higher, led by active bargain-hunting in small and medium-sized shares, brokers said.
But they warned that the climb was a technical rebound after previous sharp falls in the index and would be difficult to sustain.
"It's too early to say the market has turned around, it's more of a technical rebound from the eight-day fall we had," said Bae Kyoung-jin of Seoul Securities.
The market gained 10.28 points to provisionally end at 767.87. Advancers swamped decliners 725 to 166.

Sentiment improved on hopes of interest rate cuts. The reserve requirement ratio for banks will fall to an average 5.5 percent from November 8. Despite a huge volume of bond issues expected this month, 3.1 trillion won worth, investors are hoping that rates will fall.

But brokers said that an overhang of loans for margin trading would limit a sharp rise. Loans for margin trading are at about three trillion won, while customer deposits at brokerage houses lag behind at around 2.7 trillion. Analysts have said that 200-900 billion won in loans will have to be paid back in November.
Trading was active, with 29.18 million shares changing hands.
Shares that were seen to be relatively cheap profited from bargain hunting. Dong Sung shares topped the most actives list, gaining 260 won to 4,870. Il Sung Construction rose 430 won to 10,300.
Samsung Electronics, whose shares have been battered by uncertainty over falling semiconductor prices, gained 3,400 won to 61,500.
December futures rose 0.55 of a point to 82.45, while the KOSPI 200 index rose 1.15 points to 80.22.
